content.text:
Boosting Agentic AI Throughput with Intel® Xeon® CPUs: Intel reports Xeon 6-based instances delivered higher normalized task throughput than the tested 5th Gen AMD EPYC and Arm v9.2A instances across healthcare, banking/financial services, and manufacturing tasks. It describes a deterministic Terminal-Bench 2.0 replay, 24-way concurrency, a 60-minute window, and a whole-box tasks-per-60-minutes metric. Intel identifies the configurations as AWS instances with 48 vCPU and 185 GB memory and says testing was in September 2026. (time=2026-10-06T17:04:14Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Intel Corporation (via Public) / Boosting Agentic AI Throughput with Intel Xeon CPUs: The search-result record says Intel published the content on October 6 and that it was distributed via Public Technologies at 17:05 UTC, unedited and unaltered. It reproduces the benchmark claims and methodology. This is a syndication of Intel’s disclosure, not independent testing or editorial corroboration. (time=2026-10-06T17:05Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Intel Newsroom | News and Information: The current newsroom index lists the benchmark article and other Intel items dated October 6, including a software article and a Q3-results-date notice. The index supplies dates, not clock times, and cannot establish whether those other items were public by the cutoff. (time=UNKNOWN; cutoff=UNKNOWN).
